You are an expert e-commerce logistics & order management system designer.

Enhance the existing VexoKart app by implementing a Meesho-style Shipping Label system.
Do NOT delete or overwrite any existing data (users, vendors, products, orders).

=================================
WHEN TO GENERATE SHIPPING LABEL
=================================
• Label is generated ONLY after:
  Vendor clicks “Mark as Packed”
• Label is auto-linked to that order

=================================
SHIPPING LABEL (PRINTABLE)
=================================
Generate a professional, courier-ready shipping label (A4 & thermal compatible).

---------------------------------
TOP HEADER
---------------------------------
• VexoKart logo
• Order Type badge:
   - COD / PREPAID (clearly visible)
• Order ID (large & bold)
• Order Date

---------------------------------
QR CODE (CENTER)
---------------------------------
Generate a scannable QR code containing:
{
  order_id,
  user_id,
  vendor_id,
  payment_mode,
  order_total,
  current_status
}

Courier scan must open order tracking page.

---------------------------------
BUYER / USER DETAILS (MANDATORY)
---------------------------------
Show clearly on label:

• Customer Name
• Customer Phone Number
• Customer Email (optional)
• Full Shipping Address
   - House / Street
   - Area / Landmark
   - City
   - State
   - Pincode

Label must clearly show:
“DELIVER TO (CUSTOMER)”

---------------------------------
SELLER / VENDOR DETAILS
---------------------------------
• Store Name
• Vendor ID
• Pickup Address
• Vendor Phone Number

Label must clearly show:
“SHIP FROM (SELLER)”

---------------------------------
PRODUCT DETAILS
---------------------------------
• Product Name(s)
• Variant (Color / Size)
• Quantity
• SKU / Product ID
• Total Items Count

---------------------------------
PAYMENT DETAILS
---------------------------------
• Item Total
• Shipping Charges
• Discount (if any)
• Final Payable Amount
• COD Amount (if COD)
• Payment Status:
   - Paid / Cash on Delivery

---------------------------------
BARCODE / LABEL META
---------------------------------
• Shipment ID
• Generated Date & Time
• VexoKart Support ID

=================================
COURIER SCAN FLOW
=================================
When courier scans QR:

• Show order summary
• Allow status update:
   ☐ Picked Up
   ☐ In Transit
   ☐ Out for Delivery
   ☐ Delivered
   ☐ Cancelled / RTO

Each update must:
• Save to orders.status
• Append to orders.status_history
• Timestamp + actor (courier)

=================================
DATABASE REQUIREMENTS
=================================
Ensure these columns exist (add if missing):

orders:
- label_url
- status
- status_history (JSON)
- shipping_address (JSON)
- user_id
- vendor_id
- payment_mode
- total_amount

=================================
NOTIFICATIONS
=================================
On every status change:
• User receives in-app notification
• Vendor receives in-app notification
• Admin dashboard updates in real-time

=================================
DESIGN RULES
=================================
• Print-friendly black & white layout
• Clear section dividers
• Looks like Meesho / Flipkart label
• Mobile scan + PDF print ready

=================================
IMPORTANT
=================================
• Never delete existing orders
• Never change existing order IDs
• Label must always show CUSTOMER DETAILS clearly

**Implementing Label System**

I'm currently focused on the label generation aspect, triggered by the vendor's "Mark as Packed" action. The core functionality seems straightforward. I need to determine the optimal structure for the printable labels, and I'm leaning toward a design similar to Meesho's. This includes essential details such as shipping address, order ID, product information, and barcodes.


**Defining Label Specifications**

I've fleshed out the label design, aiming for a professional black and white layout similar to Meesho and Flipkart. I've considered A4 and thermal (4x6) paper support. The structure includes header with logo, order ID, QR code, buyer and seller details, product information (names, quantities, SKUs), payment breakdown, and crucial barcodes. I'm also planning the courier's scanning flow.


**Integrating Order Updates**

I'm now integrating notifications for status changes, targeting both users and vendors. This includes refining the mobile-first UI/UX with dark/light theme options, and simulating a print-ready PDF. I'm focusing on adapting the existing `ShippingLabelModal.tsx`, and developing triggers in `VendorOrdersPage.tsx`, plus handling status updates in `CourierScanPage.tsx`. Need to update `OrderContext.tsx` status logic too. I'm finalizing `types.ts` to include `qrToken` for secure order access in the QR code.


**Revising Label Aesthetics**

I'm now focusing on a complete visual overhaul, mirroring Meesho's label style with tabular layouts, ample barcodes, and clear "Ship From/To" sections. Simple sans-serif fonts and clear COD/Prepaid indicators are being integrated. I'm also ensuring the `CourierScanPage` handles all necessary order statuses (Picked Up, In Transit, etc.) for comprehensive tracking. The `qrToken` will be reflected correctly.


**Refining Courier Interface**

I'm currently updating the `OrderItem` type to include SKU data, ensuring that the `OrderContext` history reflects courier actions accurately. The `ShippingLabelModal` is getting a complete makeover to match Meesho's aesthetic, with a Tailwind-based design for a crisp black-and-white look. I am also working on enhancing the courier UI on the `CourierScanPage`. The label design will leverage `bwipjs-api` for barcodes and `qrserver` for QR codes, keeping the existing client-side approach.

This specification details the implementation of a professional, Meesho-inspired logistics and shipping label system for VexoKart.

### 1. Meesho-Style Shipping Label Implementation
- **Visual Appearance**: A high-contrast, black-and-white, tabular layout designed for maximum legibility on both A4 and 4x6 thermal printers.
- **Header**: Features the VexoKart logo on the left and a prominent "COD" or "PREPAID" badge on the right, alongside a large, bold Order ID.
- **QR Station**: A central scannable block containing a secure URL that directs couriers to the internal Scan Station.
- **Bilateral Address Blocks**: 
    - **Deliver To**: Large font for the customer name and pincode to assist quick sorting.
    - **Ship From**: Full vendor profile details including store name and pickup address.
- **Product Inventory**: A dedicated table showing names, variants (Color/Size), quantities, and SKUs.
- **Payment Summary**: Detailed breakdown including Subtotal, Shipping (Free), and the "Final Collectible" amount (critical for COD).

### 2. Courier Scan Station
- **Behavior**: When a courier scans the QR code on the physical package, they are taken to a dedicated, mobile-optimized page.
- **Order Summary**: Shows the courier exactly what they are carrying and, most importantly, the exact COD amount to be collected if the status is "COD Pending".
- **Logistics Controls**: Large, touch-friendly buttons to update the status:
    - **Picked Up**: Updates status to "Shipped" and adds a "Warehouse Exit" entry to history.
    - **Out for Delivery**: Signals the start of the final mile.
    - **Delivered**: Marks the order as complete and triggers the customer review flow.
    - **Refused / RTO**: Handles Return-to-Origin scenarios.

### 3. Fulfillment Flow
- **Automation**: The "Pack & Label" button becomes available to vendors once an order is "Confirmed". Clicking it generates the label data, creates the secure scan token, and sets the order to "Packed".
- **Real-time Sync**: Every logistics update by a courier triggers an in-app notification for the user and an audit log entry in the Admin Hub.

I have redesigned the **Fulfillment Station** (Shipping Labels) and the **Scan Station** (Courier Page) to align with standard Meesho/market-ready logistics systems.

1.  **Meesho-Style Labels**: The labels are now tabular, high-contrast B&W designs. They include large "SHIP FROM" and "DELIVER TO" blocks, a prominent "COD" or "PREPAID" indicator, and a logistics-grade QR code.
2.  **QR Integration**: The generated labels encode a secure `qrToken`. Scanning this token opens the `CourierScanPage` directly.
3.  **Logistics-First UX**: The scan page now highlights **COD amounts** in black blocks (if applicable), which is the most critical information for a courier. It allows for one-tap status updates (Picked Up, Out for Delivery, Delivered, RTO).
4.  **Audit Logs**: Every courier update is recorded in the `statusHistory` with the `Courier` actor and an optional note, ensuring a full audit trail for the vendor and customer.
5.  **Notifications**: These status changes trigger real-time in-app notifications for the buyer, maintaining trust throughout the delivery lifecycle.

payload.text:
Fix product image sizing and layout issues across the VexoKart app:

Problem:
- Product images appear oversized, stretched, or overflow cards.
- Images are not consistent across home, category, and product detail pages.

Requirements:
1) Enforce a fixed aspect ratio for all product images (1:1 square).
2) Apply `object-fit: cover` to all product images so they crop correctly without distortion.
3) Set a max height and width for product images:
   - Home & Category cards: 160px height
   - Product detail main image: 320px height
4) Ensure images never overflow their card container.
5) Add rounded corners to images for a clean UI.
6) Center images inside cards vertically and horizontally.
7) Lazy load product images to improve performance.
8) Fallback image:
   - If product image fails to load, show a default placeholder image.
9) Multiple images support:
   - Show only the first image on home/category cards.
   - Show image gallery slider on product detail page.
10) Ensure responsive behavior:
    - Images adapt correctly on mobile, tablet, and desktop.

CSS / UI Rules:
- Use consistent image container class across app.
- Prevent layout shift when images load.
- Do not stretch images under any condition.

Goal:
All product images must look clean, professional, uniform, and perfectly fitted like Amazon / Myntra product cards.

**Implementing Image Fixes**

I'm currently working on addressing image sizing problems in VexoKart. The focus is now on fixing visual inconsistencies on the home page and product details. We'll enforce a 1:1 square aspect ratio for all images to prevent distortions. `object-fit: cover` will be key. Home and category cards will get a 160px max height, and the product detail main image will be 320px.


**Revising Image Standards**

I've been meticulously reviewing the image handling across the VexoKart app.  I'm adapting to the square aspect ratio, targeting the `ProductCard` and detail pages. Height adjustments for the home and category cards and the product detail main image are also being fine-tuned. Lazy loading, error fallback, and gallery integration on the detail page are also in scope. I'm focusing on a mobile-first, responsive strategy with consistent classes to avoid layout shifting.


**Defining Image Sizes**

I'm solidifying image dimensions across the app. Considering mobile-first, I've decided a 320px square image will work great as the product hero. I'm updating `ProductCard.tsx` to a square aspect ratio with `max-h-[160px]` and adding lazy loading and a fallback image. I'm also revising the gallery container in `ProductDetailPage.tsx` for similar adjustments, ensuring consistent sizing and a better user experience.


**Finalizing Image Dimensions**

I'm now implementing the 320x320 image size for product heroes, extending it to the `ProductCard` component, and updating `ProductDetailPage` to ensure this consistent size. I've updated the `Skeleton` component to reflect this change. I'm also addressing lazy loading and fallback images for the slider images and ensuring the fallback displays as expected. I'm now turning my focus to updating the home and products pages.


**Optimizing Image Grid**

I'm now revising my approach to the home and category cards. The "Home & Category cards: 160px height" specification has led me to rethink the use of a fixed height within a responsive grid. I'm prioritizing `aspect-square` with `h-40` or `max-h-[160px]` to ensure optimal responsiveness and prevent potential issues with variable widths. I am aiming for 1:1 up to 160px on smaller screens. I'm focusing on refining the code changes to implement this strategy.

payload.text:
Fix vendor, orders, and invoice linkage issues.

Requirements:
1. Ensure products table contains vendor_id.
2. Ensure orders table contains vendor_id (bigint).
3. When creating an order, always save:
   orders.vendor_id = products.vendor_id.
4. Update vendor dashboard orders query to:
   fetch only orders where orders.vendor_id = currentVendorId.
5. Update invoice API to JOIN vendors table:
   orders.vendor_id → vendors.id.
6. Display vendors.store_name as "Sold by" in invoice.
7. Remove hardcoded "Unknown Seller".

Expected Result:
- Vendor sees only their own orders.
- Invoice shows correct vendor store name.
- Product page, vendor dashboard, and invoice remain consistent.

**Refining the Database Design**

I've been wrestling with the database schema. My main focus is on orders and how they relate to vendors and invoices within the React + Supabase application. I've concluded that orders need a clear link to the specific vendors they're purchasing from. I'm also examining how invoices currently function to ensure they align with the proposed changes.


**Integrating Vendor Information**

I'm currently addressing the "Unknown Seller" issue, realizing it stems from missing vendor data links.  The vendor dashboard requires filtering to only display relevant orders. Moreover, I plan to incorporate the `store_name` from the `vendors` table in invoices.  The design for data typing must be updated in `types.ts` and in `OrderContext.tsx` to handle vendor IDs for clarity.


**Clarifying Order-Vendor Linking**

My current thinking centers on solidifying the link between orders and vendors.  I'm focusing on ensuring the `vendor_id` is correctly transferred during order creation, particularly from the product data within the cart. This involves updating `CheckoutPage.tsx` to include the `vendor_id` in the order payload.  I'm also considering how to best display vendor information in the invoice modal, ensuring a dynamic rather than hardcoded display by leveraging existing context or potential API enhancements.


**Revising Invoice Data Retrieval**

I'm now focusing on improving how invoice data is retrieved, leveraging Supabase's join functionality. This will allow me to include the vendor's `store_name` directly in the invoice.  The changes involve updating the query in `OrderContext.tsx` to include a join with the `vendors` table, so the invoice will display a 'Sold by' vendor name. I plan to refine the query using the suggested syntax: `?select=*,vendor:vendors(*)` or a similar approach for clarity.


**Analyzing Vendor ID Handling**

I'm now grappling with the `vendor_id` implications for multi-vendor orders, reconciling the single `vendor_id` concept with a marketplace model. My current plan is to handle multi-vendor scenarios by potentially splitting orders or storing a primary vendor ID. I will update the `refreshOrders` query to include vendor details and adjust `addOrder` to send the `vendor_id`. Also, I'll update the components related to displaying and filtering vendor data.


**Updating Data Type Alignment**

I'm currently working to align the data types for vendor IDs across my React application and the Supabase database. I've pinpointed an inconsistency where the `vendor_id` is defined as a `string` in `types.ts` for products and orders, but a `number` for vendors. My plan involves correcting this by making `Order.vendor_id` a `number` to match the database's `bigint` type, ensuring consistency across the application. I'll be updating `OrderContext.tsx`, `CheckoutPage.tsx`, and `VendorOrdersPage.tsx` to reflect this change. I'm also ensuring the invoice now includes the vendor's `store_name` by leveraging a join in the Supabase query.

<specification>
To resolve the disconnect between vendors, orders, and invoices, the following production-grade updates will be implemented:

1.  **Database Integration & Join Logic**:
    *   Update `OrderContext.tsx` to use Supabase's relational embedding. The fetch query will now request `vendors(store_name)` alongside order data.
    *   Normalize `vendor_id` handling across the application to ensure numeric compatibility (BigInt).

2.  **Order Creation Fix**:
    *   Modify `CheckoutPage.tsx` to extract the primary numeric `vendor_id` from cart items.
    *   Update `OrderContext.tsx`'s `addOrder` function to persist the `vendor_id` as a top-level column in the `orders` table, facilitating indexed lookups for vendor dashboards.

3.  **Invoice & My Orders UI Enhancement**:
    *   `InvoiceModal.tsx` will be updated to display the `store_name` retrieved from the joined vendor record. This eliminates "Unknown Seller" by relying on a single source of truth (the Vendors table).
    *   `MyOrdersPage.tsx` will be enhanced to show the verified store name of the seller.

4.  **Vendor Dashboard & Fulfillment**:
    *   `VendorOrdersPage.tsx` and `VendorDashboardPage.tsx` will be updated to filter data based on the numeric `vendor_id` column, ensuring vendors strictly see their own transaction history.

5.  **Data Consistency**:
    *   Remove hardcoded platform names ("VexoKart Direct") in favor of dynamic store name resolution from the joined vendor profile.
</specification>

### Integration Instructions

#### 1. Paste the API Key
You should paste your Fast2SMS API Key in the **environment variables** of your hosting platform (e.g., Vercel, Netlify, or your `.env` file) as:
`FAST2SMS_API_KEY=your_actual_key_here`

The application logic automatically looks for this variable in `process.env.FAST2SMS_API_KEY`. If not found, it defaults to the value stored in the admin settings.

#### 2. How to Test SMS Events
You can test each event directly within the app UI:

1.  **User Login Success**: 
    - Simply log out and log back into any existing account (or a new one). 
    - Ensure the user profile has a valid phone number. 
    - Check the **Admin Hub > Notification Hub > Audit Logs** to see the Fast2SMS delivery status.

2.  **Order Placed Successfully**:
    - Add an item to your cart and complete the checkout process (either via Razorpay Test/Live or COD).
    - An SMS is triggered immediately after the "Order Success" screen appears.

3.  **Order Cancelled**:
    - Go to **Profile > My Orders**.
    - Click on an active order (status 'Placed' or 'Confirmed').
    - Click the **Cancel Order** button at the top right.
    - Confirm the cancellation. An SMS alert will be dispatched stating the order has been revoked.

All delivery attempts, including success/failure responses from Fast2SMS, are visible in real-time under the **Admin Hub > Notification Hub**.

payload.text:
You are a senior full-stack engineer.

TASK:
Implement a complete notification system in VexoKart (Amazon-style).

REQUIREMENTS:

1. DATABASE
Use table `notifications` with fields:
- user_id
- vendor_id
- role (user | vendor | admin)
- title
- message
- type
- is_read
- created_at

2. WHEN TO CREATE NOTIFICATIONS

A) Order Placed
- User → "Your order has been placed successfully"
- Vendor → "You received a new order"
- Admin → "New order received"

B) Payment Success
- User → "Payment successful for Order #{order_id}"
- Admin → "Payment received"

C) Order Shipped
- User → "Your order has been shipped"
- Vendor → "Order shipped successfully"

D) Order Delivered
- User → "Your order has been delivered"

3. HOW TO CREATE
- On each event, insert row into `notifications`
- Use Supabase insert (no localStorage)
- Notifications must persist after refresh

4. UI
- Bell icon on header
- Show unread count badge
- Notification panel:
  - Title
  - Message
  - Time (relative)
- Clicking notification marks it as read

5. FILTERING
- User sees only role='user' notifications
- Vendor sees role='vendor'
- Admin sees role='admin'

6. REAL-TIME (OPTIONAL)
- Use Supabase Realtime to auto-update notification list

7. ERROR HANDLING
- If notification insert fails, log error silently
- Do not block order flow

IMPORTANT:
- No hardcoded data
- Use proper foreign keys (user_id / vendor_id)
- Notifications must not duplicate

**Constructing Notification System**

I'm now focusing on the database structure for notifications, specifically the 'notifications' table. I've outlined the core fields needed: user and vendor IDs, a role designation, title and message content, a notification type, read status, and a creation timestamp. Next, I'll be defining the trigger points for these notifications; I'm starting with Order Placement, Payment Success, and Order Shipment, as the initial priorities.


**Developing Notification Logic**

I've been mapping out the notifications system further, focusing on database interaction and UI. The design now specifies Supabase inserts, not local storage, for persistence. I'm building out filtering by role. The UI will feature a header bell and an unread count. I'm preparing to modify `types.ts` and `NotificationContext.tsx` to handle fetching, reading, and creating notifications from the new table and hook into the appropriate order events to trigger new notifications.


**Refining Notification Methods**

I'm now honing the `NotificationContext`'s methods. I'm focusing on transitioning the logic from the old `notifications_log` table to the new `notifications` table. I'm building out the calls to `createNotification` and REST API `GET` calls with the role based filters for each of the entities (user, vendor, admin). I'm targeting the order lifecycle to create the three notification objects. I am in the final stages of defining the `AppNotification` interface in `types.ts`, and I'm updating the Header component to display an unread notification count.


**Defining Notification Endpoints**

I'm now integrating notification endpoints with PostgREST. I've defined `createAppNotification` as an internal helper for inserts and `markAsRead` to update the read status with a PATCH. I'm focusing on user role and ID when fetching notifications. The app uses `BASE_API_URL` which is Supabase PostgREST, so I'm writing the XML.

You are a senior full-stack engineer.

Fix the shipping label system end-to-end. 
Currently, labels bucket exists but PDF files are not uploaded, causing “Object not found”.

GOAL:
When an order is confirmed:
1) Generate a shipping label PDF
2) Upload it to Supabase Storage
3) Save the public URL in orders.label_url
4) Make the label accessible to vendor, admin, and invoice view

TECH STACK:
- Frontend: React
- Backend: Supabase
- Storage: Supabase Storage
- Bucket: labels (PUBLIC)
- Orders table has column: label_url (text)

IMPLEMENT EXACTLY THIS FLOW:

1. SHIPPING LABEL DATA
Generate PDF using order data:
- Order ID
- User full name
- Phone
- Full address (street, city, state, pincode)
- Vendor store_name
- COD / ONLINE
- Total amount
- QR code (order_id)

2. PDF GENERATION
Use jsPDF (or equivalent) to generate a PDF blob.

3. UPLOAD TO SUPABASE STORAGE
Upload the PDF file like this:
- bucket: labels
- file path: labels/{order_id}.pdf
- contentType: application/pdf
- upsert: true

IMPORTANT:
The file MUST be uploaded before generating URL.

4. GET PUBLIC URL
After upload, get public URL using:
storage.from("labels").getPublicUrl("labels/{order_id}.pdf")

5. SAVE URL IN DATABASE
Update orders table:
- label_url = public_url
- status = 'packed'

6. ERROR HANDLING
If upload fails:
- Do NOT save URL
- Show exact Supabase error in console

7. UI FIX
- Vendor dashboard should show “Generate Label” button
- Clicking generates + uploads label
- Show “Download Label” once label_url exists

8. DO NOT:
- Do NOT hardcode label URLs
- Do NOT assume file exists
- Do NOT skip upload step

9. FINAL CHECK
Opening this URL must work in browser:
https://<project-id>.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/labels/{order_id}.pdf

Deliver clean, working code with proper async/await and logs.

**Troubleshooting PDF Uploads**

I've been investigating the broken shipping label system. It appears that PDF files aren't making it into the `labels` bucket, causing "Object not found" errors. Consequently, the `label_url` field in the `orders` table lacks a valid public URL from Supabase Storage. I'm focusing on why the PDF generation step isn't completing as expected.


**Integrating PDF Label Generation**

I'm now integrating the label generation into the application. First, I included `jspdf` in the `index.html`. Then, I'm working on the `OrderContext.tsx` file, where I'll add a function to generate and upload the label. Inside this, I'll collect necessary order details, initialize `jsPDF`, draw the label content including text, rectangles, lines, and an image, which will then upload the generated PDF to Supabase Storage.


**Implementing PDF Uploads**

I'm making progress. I've switched gears to using `fetch` to get QR code images as blobs and then `PUT` them to Supabase Storage. I've figured out how to construct the public URLs. Next, I'll update the `VendorOrdersPage.tsx` component with a dedicated "Generate Label" button, replacing the old system.


**Defining Label Workflow**

I've nailed down the label generation process. I'm aiming to add a `generateAndUploadLabel` function to `OrderContext.tsx` which will generate PDFs using jsPDF, then upload them to Supabase Storage with the correct content type. I'll need to update the `orders` table after the upload, and also save the URL for display. Finally, in `VendorOrdersPage`, if the label isn't there, there'll be a "Generate Label" button, or "Download Label" if one exists.


**Constructing PDF URLs**

I'm now getting into the coding aspect. I'm adding `jspdf` and, more importantly, figuring out the Supabase Storage URLs. I'm choosing the direct REST approach for `OrderContext.tsx`, and I've got the public URL structure sorted. The next move is writing the actual code to bring it all together.

This specification fixes the shipping label system by implementing a complete PDF generation and storage workflow.

### Specification

1.  **PDF Generation**: Integrates `jsPDF` to construct a professional shipping label directly in the browser. The label includes the Order ID, customer details, formatted address, vendor name, payment mode, and total amount.
2.  **QR Integration**: Fetches a QR code image from `qrserver.com` containing the order payload and embeds it into the PDF.
3.  **Supabase Storage Workflow**:
    *   Converts the generated PDF into an `ArrayBuffer`.
    *   Uploads the file to the `labels` bucket at the path `labels/{order_id}.pdf` using the Supabase Storage REST API.
    *   Uses `x-upsert: true` to allow regeneration.
4.  **Database Sync**: After a successful upload, the `orders` table is updated with the new `label_url` and the status is transitioned to `Packed`.
5.  **Vendor UI Updates**: Replaces the placeholder logic with a "Confirm & Generate Label" workflow. The button dynamically switches to "Download Label" once the asset is live in Storage.

payload.text:
You are a senior Supabase + frontend engineer.

GOAL:
Fix ONLY Vendor Login, Vendor Product Save, and Vendor Dashboard sync
in the existing VexoKart app.

IMPORTANT RULES:
- Do NOT delete any existing data
- Do NOT rename tables
- Do NOT change Admin or User logic
- Fix ONLY vendor-related bugs
- Assume Supabase database already exists

================================
DATABASE STRUCTURE (EXACT)
================================

users:
- id (bigint, primary key)
- email (text)
- password (text)
- role (text) → user | vendor | admin

vendors:
- id (bigint, primary key)
- user_id (bigint, FK → users.id)
- store_name (text)
- status (text) → pending | approved | suspended

products:
- id
- vendor_id (FK → vendors.id)
- name
- price
- category_id
- images (jsonb)
- highlights (text[])
- status (text, default 'approved')

================================
VENDOR LOGIN FIX (CRITICAL)
================================

1. Vendor logs in using same login as user.
2. After auth success:
   - Check users.role === 'vendor'
   - If not vendor → block vendor access.

3. Fetch vendor ONLY like this:
   vendors.user_id = auth.user.id

   ❌ NEVER use email
   ❌ NEVER use localStorage email

4. If vendor not found:
   - Show: "Vendor profile not found"
   - Logout vendor

5. If vendor.status !== 'approved':
   - Show: "Vendor not approved"
   - Block dashboard

================================
PRODUCT ADD FIX
================================

When vendor adds product:
- Always set products.vendor_id = vendors.id
- Save images as JSON array
- Do NOT overwrite vendor_id
- Do NOT auto-delete product after save

================================
VENDOR DASHBOARD FIX
================================

Vendor dashboard must:
- Fetch products where products.vendor_id = vendors.id
- Fetch orders containing vendor products only
- Show correct:
  - Total Products
  - Orders Count
  - Revenue (sum of order items)

================================
SYNC / TIMEOUT FIX
================================

- Do NOT query dashboard before vendor profile loads
- Add loading state
- Wrap all Supabase calls in try/catch
- Log exact Supabase error in console

================================
EXPECTED RESULT
================================

✔ Vendor login works
✔ Product save stays permanent
✔ Vendor dashboard shows products
✔ No sync timeout
✔ No data loss

You are a senior Supabase backend engineer.

TASK:
Restore the shipping label system EXACTLY as it was working earlier.
Do NOT redesign, do NOT change UI.
Just FIX the broken logic.

CURRENT PROBLEM:
- Shipping label URL returns 404 "Object not found"
- Supabase Storage bucket not found
- Label PDF not accessible
- Previously working label system must be restored

==============================
STORAGE FIX (CRITICAL)
==============================

1. Ensure Supabase Storage bucket exists with EXACT name:
   bucket name: labels

2. Bucket must be:
   - Public
   - File type: PDF
   - Path format:
     labels/{order_id}.pdf

3. If bucket does not exist:
   - Create bucket "labels"
   - Set public = true

4. NEVER change bucket name again.

==============================
LABEL GENERATION LOGIC
==============================

On order confirmation:

- Generate PDF shipping label
- Save it to:
  Supabase Storage → labels/{order_id}.pdf

- Store URL in orders table:
  orders.label_url = public URL of PDF

URL FORMAT (IMPORTANT):
https://<project-id>.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/labels/{order_id}.pdf

==============================
LABEL CONTENT (RESTORE OLD FORMAT)
==============================

Label must include:

- VEXOKART header
- Order ID
- Barcode + QR
- SELLER (vendor):
  - store_name
  - address
  - phone

- CUSTOMER:
  - full name
  - phone
  - full address
  - pincode

- PAYMENT MODE:
  - COD or ONLINE

- TOTAL AMOUNT
- GST if applicable

Layout must remain same as earlier (Meesho style).

==============================
DATABASE REQUIREMENTS
==============================

orders table MUST have:
- id
- user_id
- vendor_id
- shipping_address (json)
- payment_mode
- total
- label_url (text)

DO NOT rename columns.

==============================
ERROR HANDLING
==============================

If label generation fails:
- Show exact Supabase error in console
- Do NOT silently fail
- Do NOT delete order

==============================
EXPECTED RESULT
==============================

✔ Old shipping label works again
✔ PDF opens in browser
✔ No 404 error
✔ Same label design as before
✔ Vendor + user details visible

OUTPUT:
Restore label system exactly as before. No new features.

I've discovered the root cause of the upload path errors. The label generation process was incorrectly prepending "labels/" to the order ID, resulting in broken URLs. My immediate task involves correcting the path logic in `context/OrderContext.tsx` and ensuring that PDFs upload directly to `{order_id}.pdf` within the public `labels` bucket. The pdfs still need to include the data, so I have to verify the data in the PDF includes the required fields (VEXOKART header, Order ID, Barcode, QR, Seller details (store name, address, phone), Customer details (name, phone, address, pincode), Payment mode, Total amount).


**Verifying File Pathing**

I've just been reviewing the bucket file pathing logic, and I realize there's a discrepancy. I need to make sure the label URLs are correct. I need to check the exact file path inside the bucket, ensuring it's just `{order_id}.pdf`. The public URL path should then be correctly formatted as `.../public/labels/{order_id}.pdf`. I also need to verify existing buckets or create them if necessary, but assume permissions are set up. Finally, I'll update the `label_url` in the `orders` table.


**Resolving File Mismatch**

I've just cleared up a pathing discrepancy. Initially, the file path `{order_id}.pdf` in the `labels` bucket conflicted with the implied public URL, but now I will ensure the public URLs will match the file path in the `labels` bucket. I'm focusing on file generation using `jsPDF` for the PDF, and integrating both QR codes from `qrserver.com` and barcodes via `bwipjs-api`. Additionally, I will update `context/OrderContext.tsx` and `pages/vendor/VendorOrdersPage.tsx`, using `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_KEY` from `constants.ts`. The implementation will handle `upsert: true` with content type `application/pdf`. The PDFs will contain the specified fields.


**Reconciling Label Paths**

I've just run into a slight inconsistency. My storage calls and public URLs don't align. After some thought, I've resolved this by aligning the bucket and path, confirming that `.../public/labels/labels/{order_id}.pdf` is the intended URL format, as this aligns with the previous code. Now, I need to make sure the label URLs are correct.


**Finalizing Path Structure**

I'm now ensuring the path inside the `labels` bucket is just `{order_id}.pdf`. I'll align with the "FINAL CHECK" URL format for consistent Supabase storage referencing. I'm restoring the code in `generateAndUploadLabel` within `OrderContext.tsx` and the button logic in `VendorOrdersPage.tsx`. Currently I'm looking into the usage of `jsPDF` to make sure fonts and styles are clean. I need to make sure the implementation generates the PDF, uploads to Supabase using the REST API, and updates the database. Also, I'll confirm the `orders` table structure includes `total` (previously using `total_amount` or `total`), along with the other required fields.

To restore the shipping label system and fix the 404 "Object not found" errors, we will implement the storage upload logic strictly following the Supabase Storage REST API requirements.

### Specification
1.  **Storage Restoration**: Re-establishes the `labels` bucket as the target. The file path is set to `{order_id}.pdf` inside the `labels` bucket to satisfy the public URL format requirements.
2.  **PDF Generation (Meesho Style)**: Restores the professional layout including:
    *   **Header**: High-impact "VexoKart Logistics" branding.
    *   **Seller/Customer Blocks**: Detailed address information fetched from order and vendor profiles.
    *   **Visual IDs**: Barcode (Code128) and QR Code (Order payload) for scan-ability.
    *   **Billing details**: Subtotal, GST, and Total Payable.
3.  **End-to-End Workflow**:
    *   Generates PDF blob using `jsPDF`.
    *   Uploads to Supabase Storage with `upsert: true` and `application/pdf` content-type.
    *   Retrieves the standard public URL.
    *   Updates the `orders` table column `label_url` and transitions status to `Packed`.
